old.H2-P2: People sometimes buy forty acres and then bring all their unprocessed baggage with them to a more scenic location. The view's better, I'll give them that! But now the conflict has goats.
old.H2-P3: The inner pl/ork can start right where you live, though. [Peer counseling](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/p/hearthwork-an-integrated-peer-counseling) only needs two people and enough privacy to talk. And reparenting, somatic work, jealousy, conflict repair, etc etc? None of that has to wait for a deed either!
old.H2-P4: A group that practices together weekly for two years may never own land. So what? It can still make a difference in how people get through divorce, illness, grief, parenting and plain old loneliness.
old.H3-P4: Where do you find them? Are there any unprogrammed Quaker meetings or restorative-practice groups near you? Any open-hearted congregations? Maybe a mature recovery group, or a meditation group? Or someone who came back from a long retreat kinder, rather than more impressed with themselves?
old.H3-P5: Have you ever visited an actual community? Go! [Twin Oaks](https://twinoaks.org/), [East Wind](http://eastwind.org/), [Acorn](https://www.ic.org/directory/acorn-community-farm/) and other [intentional communities](https://www.ic.org/) take visitors, and so do a lot of [ecovillages](https://ecovillage.org/). Just check their current visitor requirements first.
old.H3-P6: What do you get out of a visit? Things no manifesto can tell you. How much togetherness you actually enjoy, for one, and what kind of privacy you need. And which labor system drives you nuts! And whether communal showers feel liberating or send you off pricing studio apartments.
